attribution.note: Zitron wrote this in his own post, in his own voice.

semantics.note: The surrounding argument is about expectations, but the clause 'have yet to show meaningful improvement over the past few years' is a firm historical assertion. The normalisation captures it faithfully.

contract.note: No threshold was supplied for 'meaningful'. Reading it as substantial gains on comparable reasoning, coding and task evaluations is ordinary and fair. Using 2022 to April 2025 as 'the past few years' is reasonable.

evidence.note: The METR preprint was published 2025-03-18, before the post. It is an independent longitudinal measure showing frontier time horizons doubling about every seven months since 2019. The task set is narrow but has practical relevance.

The AI Index chapter was available 2025-04-07. It reports large gains: MMMU +18.8 points, GPQA +48.9 points, SWE-bench from 4.4% to 71.7% (2023 to 2024). These are system-level results, but they are still substantial capability gains.

METR's original summary notes poor reliability on low-skill autonomous work alongside rapid gains. It supports the point about limitations, not stagnation. The page snapshot carries later headers, but the quoted passage is the original text.

reviews.rationale: Independent longitudinal evaluations published before the post (METR, AI Index 2025) show substantial gains on reasoning, coding and task-completion benchmarks. Persistent limitations (e3) do not establish an absence of meaningful improvement. Under the fair plain reading, the claim of no meaningful improvement is contradicted.

semantics.note: The proposition is close to verbatim. Only the $50 billion industry size is checkable; 'masquerading as a trillion-dollar panacea' is rhetoric.

contract.note: The post sits beside a discussion of annualized company AI revenue, so reading the figure as annualized revenue in Q1 2025 is ordinary. Scope, the treatment of hardware, and the tolerance were not supplied by the speaker, so the result depends on the evaluator's choices.

evidence.note: Microsoft's self-reported $13B AI run rate from January 2025. This is one company's figure on a different scope, so it cannot establish the industry total.

reviews.rationale: The packet contains no industry-wide estimate that matches the contract's scope, window and annualized revenue basis. One company's run rate is context only. The evidence available does not settle whether the industry was about $50B.

attribution.note: Zitron wrote this in his own post, in his own voice.

semantics.note: 'Only get more expensive' is a present-tense generalization about a trend in recent models, which makes it an observation. GPT-4.5 is the speaker's example, not the whole scope of the claim.

contract.note: The speaker supplied the per-token API prices himself, so API pricing is a fair measure. The surrounding text also mentions inference costs, but the explicit example anchors the reading. Treating 'only' as allowing counterexamples is ordinary.

evidence.note: OpenAI's dated price list of 2025-04-14 shows GPT-4.1 cheaper than GPT-4o. A company's own published prices are authoritative for its prices. This was a newer major model released before the post at lower prices.
GPT-4.5 (February 2025) was more expensive than GPT-4o. This supports the speaker's example but does not show a consistent upward trend.

reviews.rationale: Two weeks before the post, OpenAI released GPT-4.1 at prices below GPT-4o and called GPT-4.1 nano its cheapest model ever. That is the contract's counterexample. GPT-4.5 being expensive does not rescue the claim that the latest models 'only' get more expensive.

semantics.note: Faithful to the source. 'If I'm honest' is rhetorical. The second clause is an interpretive judgment framed as a sign, and the revision correctly avoids recasting it as causal.

contract.note: The post's own explanation fairly defines processing as interpreting intent. The April 2025 window and the threshold for 'meaningful innovation' are evaluator choices, so the result depends on interpretation.

evidence.note: A 2023 experiment on older tools that measured broad task outcomes. It found no significant overall performance difference and does not isolate intent interpretation in April 2025.
Google's own April 2025 announcement of multimodal AI Mode. It is a company disclosure of a feature, not an independent finding of meaningful improvement or of parity with ChatGPT.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no contemporaneous, identical-query comparison that isolates intent interpretation, and no independent evidence on whether Google's changes were meaningful. The relevant comparisons could not be read. Neither part of the claim is settled.
